===== chart.py
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

data = {
    'Country': [
        'Armenia', 'Micronesia', 'Timor-Leste', 'Ethiopia', 'Bhutan',
        'Laos', 'Nepal', 'Cambodia', 'Kenya', 'Rwanda'
    ],
    '2010': [12, 18, 15, 10, 25, 20, 18, 22, 28, 30],
    '2012': [18, 25, 22, 18, 30, 30, 28, 30, 35, 38],
    '2014': [25, 35, 30, 28, 40, 45, 37, 40, 42, 45],
    '2016': [45, 65, 55, 48, 50, 55, 55, 60, 52, 58],
    '2018': [55, 65, 55, 60, 58, 65, 65, 70, 60, 65]
}

df = pd.DataFrame(data)
df.set_index('Country', inplace=True)

categories = list(df.columns)
N = len(categories)

angles = [n / float(N) * 2 * np.pi for n in range(N)]
angles += angles[:1]

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 8), subplot_kw=dict(polar=True))

ax.set_theta_offset(np.pi / 2)
ax.set_theta_direction(-1)

plt.xticks(angles[:-1], categories)

ax.set_rlabel_position(0)
plt.yticks([10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70], ["10%", "20%", "30%", "40%", "50%", "60%", "70%"], color="grey", size=9)
plt.ylim(0, 70)

colors = [
    '#4E79A7', '#F28E2B', '#E15759', '#76B7B2', '#59A14F',
    '#EDC948', '#B07AA1', '#FF9DA7', '#9C755F', '#BAB0AC'
]

for idx, (country, row) in enumerate(df.iterrows()):
    values = row.tolist()
    values += values[:1]
    ax.plot(angles, values, linewidth=2, linestyle='solid', label=country, color=colors[idx])
    ax.fill(angles, values, color=colors[idx], alpha=0.25)

plt.title('Contraceptive Prevalence Rates by Country (2010-2018)', size=15, y=1.1)
ax.legend(loc='upper right', bbox_to_anchor=(1.3, 1.1))

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig("output.png")

The image is a radar chart titled "Contraceptive Prevalence Rates by Country (2010-2018)." This type of chart displays multivariate data in a two-dimensional format, where each axis represents a different year spanning from 2010 to 2018. The chart features ten distinct countries, each represented by a uniquely colored line and filled area, creating a visual comparison of contraceptive prevalence rates over the given years.

The radial axes are labeled with percentage values ranging from 10% to 70%, indicating the prevalence rates. Each country's data forms a polygonal shape, with vertices marking the prevalence rates for the years 2010, 2012, 2014, 2016, and 2018.

Armenia, shown in blue, starts at 12% in 2010, gradually increasing to 55% by 2018. Micronesia, represented in orange, begins at 18% in 2010 and reaches 65% in 2018, showing a significant rise. Timor-Leste, depicted in red, starts at 15% in 2010 and also climbs to 55% by 2018. Ethiopia, illustrated in teal, has a steady increase from 10% in 2010 to 60% in 2018.

Bhutan, shown in green, starts with a 25% rate in 2010 and reaches 58% by 2018. Laos, in yellow, begins at 20% in 2010, rising to 65% in 2018. Nepal, depicted in purple, starts at 18% in 2010 and ends at 65% in 2018. Cambodia, illustrated in pink, shows an increase from 22% in 2010 to 70% by 2018, displaying the highest rates among the countries shown.

Kenya, in brown, starts at 28% in 2010 and reaches 60% in 2018. Rwanda, shown in grey, begins at 30% in 2010 and increases to 65% by 2018. The chart effectively highlights the overall upward trend in contraceptive prevalence rates across all countries over the observed period. The use of different colors for each country enhances clarity and aids in distinguishing between them.
